question: What color and dimensional limits apply to crosswalk markings, including transverse crosswalk lines?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Crosswalk markings must be white, and transverse lines are limited to a width of not less than 6 inches nor greater than 24 inches. Figure 3C-1 further shows the minimum crosswalk width of 6 feet (8 feet where the posted speed limit is 40 mph or greater at a non-intersection crosswalk), and dimensional ranges for high-visibility designs such as longitudinal bar, ladder, and bar pair crosswalks. Standards (mandatory): - "The transverse lines used to establish the limits of the ladder crosswalk shall not be less than 6 inches or greater than 24 inches in width." - The visible page containing Section 3C.03 also states: "Crosswalk markings shall be white. When used, transverse lines shall not be less than 6 inches or greater than 24 inches in width," and that the minimum width of a marked crosswalk shall be 6 feet, or 8 feet at a non-intersection crosswalk where the posted speed limit is 40 mph or greater (see [Image 2]). Guidance (recommended): - Transverse line crosswalk markings should be limited to locations controlled by traffic control signals or on approaches controlled by STOP or YIELD signs. - Where aesthetic surface treatments are used, a gap of at least one-half the width of the white transverse line, but not less than 6 inches, should separate the white crosswalk lines from the aesthetic treatment (such as unmarked pavement or a black contrast line). Options (permitted): - High-visibility crosswalk markings may be used where additional conspicuity is desired over transverse line crosswalk markings. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 3C-1 depicts the dimensional limits: transverse lines 6–24 inches wide with a 6 ft minimum crosswalk width; longitudinal bars 12–60 inches long (not to exceed 2.5 times the bar width) and 12–24 inches wide; ladder designs combining both; and bar pairs of 8–12 inch bars, with a note that the minimum crosswalk width shall be 8 feet where the posted speed limit is 40 mph or greater at a non-intersection crosswalk. - [Image 2] shows Section 3C.03 (Design of Crosswalk Markings) with the Standard that crosswalk markings shall be white, transverse lines shall be 6–24 inches wide, and minimum crosswalk widths of 6 feet (8 feet at high-speed non-intersection locations), along with Figure 3C-1. - [Image 3] shows Sections 3C.04 and 3C.05, confirming that the transverse line design consists of two parallel transverse lines and that high-visibility designs (longitudinal bar, ladder, bar pair) may be used for added conspicuity. - [Image 4] shows the table of contents locating Chapter 3C (Crosswalk Markings), Sections 3C.01–3C.12. - [Image 5] shows Section 3H.03 guidance on contrast gaps between white crosswalk lines and aesthetic surface treatments, including the minimum 6-inch gap recommendation. Citations: - Section 3C.07 Standard §4 (p.592) - Section 3C.04 Guidance §1 (p.591) - Section 3H.03 Guidance §11 (p.623) - Section 3C.05 Option §1 (p.591) - Section 3C.01 Support §1 (p.589) - Section 3C.01 Support §2 (p.589) - Figure 3C-1 (p.590) - Page 631 - Page 632 - Page 664
gold_answer: Crosswalk markings must be white. Where transverse lines are used, each line must be at least 6 inches and no more than 24 inches wide. Except for certain ramp-terminal cases, the marked crosswalk should be at least 6 feet wide.
